correctness.rationale: For k>=2, n and m positive binary palindromes with canonical digits and m-n=2^k, split into L(n)<=k, same-length addition, and one-digit overflow. In the short case, reflecting the set of one-bit positions in n and m repeatedly translates positive indices by a=k-L(n)+1; this forces a|k and an exact arithmetic progression of one bits, one for each divisor. In the same-length case the changed-bit carry interval is reflection invariant and must be a singleton {k}, giving L=2k+1 and a central zero-to-one toggle with 2^(k-1) choices. In the overflow case, reflecting the new top bit and the forced upper zeros, using k>=2, makes every intermediate bit of n zero; n=2^k+1 and m=2^(k+1)+1 is unique. The three length classes do not overlap; their counts give 2^(k-1)+tau(k)+1. Independent bounded enumeration reconstructed entire pair sets for k=2..5 and searched larger lengths; the proof handles all k.
